predecessors.name: Third Dynasty of Ur
predecessors.text: Assur, the city that became an independent city-state under Puzur-Ashur I

successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: the Assyrian heartland of Cliopatria's last Assyria shape, from which the Neo-Assyrian Empire expands

ledger.x: c. 2025 BC: Assur becomes an independent city-state under Puzur-Ashur I. "Assur is generally thought to have become an independent city-state under Puzur-Ashur I, who ruled c. 2025 BC" (Old Assyrian period); the Assyria infobox "Assur becomes an independent city-state: c. 2025 BC". The page gives the city, not a…

c. 1808 BC: the Amorite Shamshi-Adad I takes Assur and founds a new dynasty. "The original Assur city-state, and the Puzur-Ashur dynasty, came to an end c. 1808 BC when the city was conquered by the Amorite ruler of Ekallatum"; his own page has c. 1809 and the Old Assyrian page "c. 1808 BC".

c. 1808 BC: Shamshi-Adad I moves the capital to Subat-Enlil. He "converted it [Shekhna, today Tell Leilan] into the capital city of Assyria, and then renamed it Šubat-Enlil" c. 1808 BC; the court had been at Ekallatum. The Assyria infobox keeps Assur.
c. 1808 BC: Shekhna on the Khabur plain becomes the royal seat. The page dates the conversion of Shekhna into Subat-Enlil to c. 1808 BC and says nothing of its prior ruler.
The Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia: the pages date no conquest except Mari.
ledger.cp: Amorite and Hurrian city-states of Upper Mesopotamia

ledger.x: c. 1796 BC: Shamshi-Adad I occupies Mari. "Shamshi-Adad I seized the opportunity and occupied Mari around 1796 BC" and "put his second son, Yasmah-Adad, on the throne in Mari"; Mari stays a separate kingdom under his son, so this is a gain by the royal house.

c. 1776 BC: Shamshi-Adad I dies and the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia breaks up. "Shamshi-Adad's death c. 1776 BC led to the collapse of the kingdom"; his page: "Yasmah-Adad was soon expelled from Mari by Zimri-Lim" and "the rest of the kingdom was eventually lost during the reigns of Ishme-Dagan I and Mut-Ashkur" to…
ledger.cp: coalition of Mari, Andarig and Eshnunna

ledger.x: c. 1776 BC: Zimri-Lim expels Yasmah-Adad from Mari. Shamshi-Adad I's page: "Yasmah-Adad was soon expelled from Mari by Zimri-Lim" after the king's death c. 1776 BC; the Mari page puts Zimri-Lim's enthronement at c. 1776 BC.

c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna seizes Subat-Enlil. "In c. 1772 BC, the new king of Eshnunna, Ibal-pi-el II invaded Ishme-Dagan's kingdom, occupying Assur, Ekallatum and Qattare before seizing Shamshi-Adad's old capital at Shubut-Enlil." (Old Assyrian period).

c. 1772 BC: Eshnunna occupies Assur. "Ibal-pi-el II invaded Ishme-Dagan's kingdom" and took "Assur, Ekallatum and Qattare" (c. 1772 BC); the Shamshi-Adad I page has only "Eshnunna captured cities around Assur".

c. 1767 BC (bridged): the Eshnunna occupation of Assur ends. The Old Assyrian page does not say when Eshnunna left ("Assur at some point returned to being an independent city-state"; Hammurabi "conquered the region c. 1761 BC"); the Eshnunna page has Elam conquering Eshnunna around 1767 (Ibal-pi-El II killed c. 1765)…
The heartland widens from 25,617 km2 to 63,722 km2 in Cliopatria's -1700 shape, when "Bel-bani founded the Adaside dynasty" (c.
Cliopatria shrinks the shape at -1500 (63,722 to 35,816 km2), 70 years before the page's Mitanni date.

c. 1363 BC: Ashur-uballit I makes Assyria a territorial state again. "Assyria became an independent territorial state under Ashur-uballit I c. 1363 BC, having previously been under the suzerainty of the Mitanni kingdom" (Mitanni's hold from c. 1430). The Middle Assyrian period begins.

c. 1363 BC: Ashur-uballit I conquers "the fertile region between the Tigris, the foothills of the Taurus Mountains and the Upper Zab", which "modern historians use to mark the beginning of the Middle Assyrian period". Arrapha and Nuzi were attacked (Nuzi destroyed "in the 1330s BC or before") but "neither city was…
Adad-nirari I (c.
Shalmaneser I (c.
Tukulti-Ninurta I (c.
ledger.cp: the northern and eastern neighbours of Assyria (page silent)

ledger.x: c. 1225 BC: Tukulti-Ninurta I conquers Babylonia and takes Kashtiliash IV prisoner. "his temporary conquest of Babylonia, which became an Assyrian vassal c. 1225-1216 BC"; "conquering Babylonia c. 1225 BC".

c. 1216 BC: Babylonia throws off Assyria. A revolt of Adad-shuma-iddina "c. 1217 BC", then Adad-shuma-usur "drove the Assyrians out c. 1216 BC". Cliopatria wrongly keeps Babylonia inside the Assyria shape to -1201.

c. 1207 BC: Tukulti-Ninurta I is murdered and the court returns from Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta (capital c. 1233-1207) to Assur (infobox "Assur (c. 1207–912 BC)"). "The assassination of Tukulti-Ninurta I c. 1207 BC led to inter-dynastic conflict and a significant decline in Assyrian power."
Cliopatria's shape widens westward at -1150 (467,282 to 515,451 km2, west edge from 36.4 E to 34.9 E).
1112 BC: Tiglath-Pileser I fights the Mushki and overruns Commagene.
1055 BC: Assyria falls back to its heartland.
934 BC: Ashur-dan II begins the recovery.
912 BC: the Middle Assyrian Empire ends with the death of Ashur-dan II; the Neo-Assyrian Empire is counted from 911 (accession of Adad-nirari II).

wars.name: Shamshi-Adad I's conquests (Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia)
Eshnunna's invasion of Ishme-Dagan I's kingdom
wars.outcome: Ibal-pi-el II of Eshnunna occupied Assur, Ekallatum and Qattara.

wars.name: Hammurabi's conquest of northern Mesopotamia
wars.outcome: Hammurabi of Babylon "conquered the region c.

wars.name: Mitanni's subjugation of Assur
wars.outcome: Assur became a Mitanni vassal c.

wars.name: Adad-nirari I's Khabur campaigns
wars.outcome: Wasashatta, son of Shattuara, rebelled and was defeated; Adad-nirari I annexed several cities on the Khabur.

wars.name: Shalmaneser I's conquest of Hanigalbat
wars.outcome: After Shattuara II rebelled with Hittite help, Shalmaneser I sacked Washukanni and the remnant of Mitanni passed to Assyria.

wars.name: Battle of Nihriya
wars.outcome: Tukulti-Ninurta I "defeated the Hittites at the Battle of Nihriya c.

wars.name: Tukulti-Ninurta I's conquest of Babylonia
wars.outcome: Kashtiliash IV was taken prisoner; Babylonia was an Assyrian vassal c.

wars.name: Assyro-Babylonian wars under Ashur-resh-ishi I and Tiglath-Pileser I
wars.outcome: Ashur-resh-ishi I fought Nebuchadnezzar I over Zanqi; Tiglath-Pileser I attacked Babylon but "did not conquer Babylonia"; Ashur-bel-kala's dispute with Marduk-nadin-ahhe was "resolved diplomatically".

wars.name: Tiglath-Pileser I's campaigns
wars.outcome: Conquests from the Mushki (1112) to the Mediterranean; "ephemeral and shaky, quickly lost again" and the end of the reign a "period of retrenchment".

wars.name: Aramean invasions and the second decline
wars.outcome: Assyria lost "most of the empire's territories outside of its heartlands", partly to Aramean tribes; by 1000 BC it was "at the low point of its power"; Ashur-dan II began the recovery from 934.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier appears on the pages for any period: city-state hinterland, an Amorite kingdom, a vassal of Mitanni, and a conquest empire whose edges are approximate.
